jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Head Count
jokes.joke: I grew up on a farm before becoming a flight attendant. The first time another attendant asked, “Chicken or beef?” I instinctively looked down the aisle for an open gate. On a farm, that’s not dinner service—that’s an inventory emergency.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Seatback Farm
jokes.joke: I grew up on a farm, so airplane safety demonstrations don't scare me. Lady's up there going 'in case of water landing, your seat cushion becomes a flotation device.' I've delivered a calf with less equipment. My dad once fixed a tractor with a seatbelt and pure spite. So when the flight attendant says 'ensure your seatback is in the upright position,' I hear my father yelling 'if it's not upright, MAKE it upright,' and honestly? Same energy, worse pay.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.model: Gemini 3.8 Flash web (joke); Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite web (judge fallback)
jokes.title: Down on the Tarmac
jokes.joke: I grew up on a dairy farm, so whenever a flight attendant starts demonstrating how the oxygen mask drops from the ceiling, my muscle memory kicks in and I immediately reach up to try and milk it.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.model: Grok Fast on grok.com (underlying model not exposed)
jokes.title: Farm Training
jokes.joke: I used to work on a farm before I became a flight attendant. Best training of my life. Now when the guy in 12B refuses to put his tray table up, I just stare him down and say, 'Buddy, I've milked things more stubborn than you.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Sky High Boundaries
jokes.joke: I once tried to be charming with a flight attendant, and she shut me down so fast the seatbelt sign came back on. I asked for a smile, and she said, “Sir, I’m not in the business of in‑flight entertainment.” I said, “Fair enough. I’m barely in the business of being a decent passenger.”

scores.comment: Several amusing farm-to-cabin parallels, but the bit sprawls and the final line is weaker than the preceding tractor image.
Very clean setup and a strong, instantly visual misdirection; concise enough that the absurd milk-the-mask turn lands sharply.
Clear and competent, but the stubborn-animal comparison is fairly obvious and the phrasing 'milked things more stubborn than you' feels slightly forced.
Readable and well-formed, but the flight-attendant comeback and self-deprecating tag are familiar and produce more of a smile than a strong laugh.
Clean farm/flight-attendant swap, solid closer, slightly telegraphed.
Absurd milking-the-mask image lands fast and clean, best turn of the batch.
Solid stubborn-tray-table line but the 'stubborn as livestock' comparison is a familiar route.
Decent back-and-forth but punchline undercuts itself rather than escalating; longer setup than payoff justifies.
Solid misdirection connecting farm inventory with airline food service, though a bit straightforward.
Strong narrative flow and great punchline pairing parental stubbornness with low airline wages.
A bit cliché on the delivery, relying on a familiar tough-attitude trope rather than a sharp observation.
Clever passenger banter, but it completely misses the premise of having a farm background.
Clear premise and serviceable farm-to-aisle image, but the inventory-emergency turn is mild and slightly explanatory.
Scattered farm comparisons dilute the timing; final payoff lands soft and over-explained.
Tight stage setup, vivid muscle-memory turn, and a clean final image that carries the laugh.
Competent self-own with a light seatbelt gag, but the disrespect concept is soft and the punch is gentle.
Clear premise; mild farm‑airline contrast, light payoff.
Good escalation and imagery; funny, slightly long.
Simple, clear gag; predictable turn.
Strong character voice; clean final line.
